=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md (and the template at workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md), live line ~94; template line ~103 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The Cloudflare Steps section invokes `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef` without `-R <owner>/<repo>`.
  WHY: CLAUDE.md §23.A explicitly notes that in Claude Code Web sessions the only git remote points at a local proxy and `gh` cannot infer the GitHub repo, so `gh run view` / `gh repo view` without `-R` fails with "failed to determine base repo". That is the exact error path this command triggers while resolving `DEPLOY_SHA`, and the result is a hard stall on the Cloudflare step before the protected-branch / pinned-worktree preflight can even run.
- changelog.d/6469-deploy-activate-credential-free-checks.md:6 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The operator-facing guidance says the command will "guide you through the step", but both command copies require the step to be marked BLOCKED and forbid providing a manual deployment command.
  WHY: An operator reading the changelog can reasonably conclude the command will walk them through a manual deploy when verification fails, contradicting the BLOCKED behavior the command text and test pin.
- changelog.d/6435-prompt-audit-claude-config.md and changelog.d/6469-deploy-activate-credential-free-checks.md; `.ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt` diff | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The PR ships two changelog fragments, while the manifest update adds only the 6435 entry.
  WHY: The release assembler treats each fragment as an independent changelog entry, and the missing 6469 manifest entry will desync the workspace inventory the orchestrator routes against.
- tests/test_deploy_activate_command.py, `test_cloudflare_preflight_and_deploy_boundaries` required-token list | PROBLEM: The test does not assert that the `gh` calls carry `-R <owner>/<repo>`.
  WHY: The same paragraph is where the missing `-R` was identified; the test would have caught the regression if it pinned the flag.
  Suggested minimal fix: add `"-R <owner>/<repo>"` (or the more specific `"gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -R"`) to the required-tuple so a future edit that drops the flag fails CI.

=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- changelog.d/6469-deploy-activate-credential-free-checks.md:6 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The release note says that if commit protection cannot be verified, `/deploy-activate` will “guide you through the step rather than deploying itself.” Both command copies instead require the step to be marked BLOCKED and forbid providing a manual deployment command.
  WHY: Operators following the release note may treat manual deployment as an allowed fallback when the documented verification gate fails.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:94; workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:103 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Both commands instruct `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef` without `-R <owner>/<repo>`.
  WHY: In Claude Code Web, the local-proxy remote does not let `gh` infer the repository. This call fails with “failed to determine base repo,” preventing the command from resolving the default branch and proceeding with deployment verification.
- changelog.d/6435-prompt-audit-claude-config.md; changelog.d/6469-deploy-activate-credential-free-checks.md:1 | severity=NIT | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The PR adds two changelog fragments, contrary to CLAUDE.md §20.B, which requires exactly one fragment per PR.
  WHY: The release assembler includes both fragments, publishing two entries for this PR instead of the single entry required by the changelog contract.

=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

  PROBLEM: The Cloudflare deploy instructions resolve the default branch with `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef` but omit the mandatory `-R shubhodeep1/coding-workflows` flag.
  WHY: In Claude Code Web, the bare `gh repo view` call fails with `failed to determine base repo`, blocking the entire Cloudflare deployment flow before `DEPLOY_SHA` is resolved.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:103 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=[5]

  PROBLEM: The fragment says "if commit protection cannot be verified, the command will guide you through the step rather than deploying itself." This implies a manual deployment fallback remains available.
  WHY: Both command copies explicitly forbid this: "mark the Cloudflare step BLOCKED in the activation log and give only a corrective verification step" and "Never emit a Worker deploy command, including one for the operator to run." The published recovery guidance contradicts the fail-closed security boundary the commands enforce.
